text:
anna: Heads up — noticed p99 spike ~15-25ms on fused-attn path after the kernel-routing heuristic change in last deploy. Repro on canary with seq_len=1024 and batch=4.

matt: ack. Do we have before/after microbench numbers? :eyes:

anna: before: p99 ~ 38ms, median ~ 12ms. after: p99 ~ 58ms, median ~ 13ms. So tail moved a lot but median stable.

raj: that smells like a tail-causing fallback or sporadic kernel mismatch causing additional copies. Any KV-cache evictions happening at the same time?

anna: checked logs, KV cache hit rate unchanged. I attached perf trace from the canary run (brief snippet):

```
# perf timeline (condensed)
0.000 - enqueue batch
0.012 - fused_flash_kernel invoked
0.013 - kernel fell back to cuBLAS path
0.060 - postprocess + memcpy
```

matt: fallback to cuBLAS at 0.013 — that explains the extra 45ms. Why is kernel-routing selecting non-flash variant for some requests?

liz: new heuristic added selection by sequence-length-quantile and current GPU utilization. If util > 70% it picks 'compatible' kernel to reduce memory pressure. Maybe on canary util spikes intermittently.

raj: but that heuristic should pick flash when seq_len >= threshold. Are we sending mixed sequence lengths in same batch? Mixed could trigger safe kernel.

anna: can repro with all seq_len=1024 single-shape batch. I instrumented kernel decision path and saw the decision came from `should_use_fused_flash=false` because `gpu_free_mem < mem_threshold` for a few iterations.

matt: what's mem_threshold? any chance recent allocator changes affect `gpu_free_mem` readings?

liz: threshold set to 2GB for fused flash. We did change async allocator commit behavior in previous PR, which can temporarily reserve memory and show less free memory even if actually available.

anna: that matches — the async allocator now holds freed buffers longer. So heuristic misreads and forces fallback, causing p99 regressions.

raj: solution options:
- relax mem check (lower threshold)
- query allocator for "allocatable" memory instead of free_memory
- make selection tolerant for short transient drops (require N consecutive low-memory samples)

matt: I'd prefer making decision based on allocatable (option 2) + a short hysteresis window (option 3). Avoid turning down threshold without data.

liz: agree. I'll open a small PR to read `allocator.allocatable_bytes()` and add a 3-sample hysteresis. Also will add a metric `kernel_choice_reason` for observability.

anna: thanks — can you add a perf unit test that toggles allocator reservation so we catch this in CI? E.g., inject fake reservation and assert selection stable for non-consecutive samples.

liz: yep will add. PR draft in ~2h.

perf-bot: perf/regression-checker found +17ms p99 on canary at 1812339900, linked run: http://ci/perf/1812339900

matt: great. Once PR lands we should run canary with synthetic load (stable util) and verify p99 returns to baseline. Also add a short rollout (5%) and monitor `kernel_choice_reason`.

anna: doing an initial rollback is ok if rollout shows user impact. For now I think fix+canary is fine.

raj: one more ask — add a microbenchmark that runs repeated fused_flash start/stop with allocator reservation toggled to ensure no oscillation.

liz: added to TODOs. will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:

anna: thanks team, saving logs to the incident folder and tagging this thread in the release notes.
